request: can you make a little scoreboard for two teams, home and away? each team needs its own button to add a point, plus a new game button that puts both back to zero, and the scores should stay saved on the server when i reload
design_rationale: A scoreboard is read from across the room, so one centred card with the two scores side by side in large tabular digits, each with its own button under it and a quieter outline New game button below; neutral base with an amber accent and nova's clean density.

verify.steps: Open the page and see Home: 0 and Away: 0, click Home scores twice and Away scores once and see Home: 2 and Away: 1, reload and still see Home: 2 and Away: 1, click New game and see Home: 0 and Away: 0.

why.services/scores.jac: Team node with a name and a score; open_scoreboard (a walker that creates Home and Away under root on first visit and reports both), add_point (a walker that takes the team name and adds one to that team only) and reset_scores (a walker that sets both to 0 and reports them).
why.components/ScoreboardPanel.jac: The whole screen: the Scoreboard heading, Home: N and Away: N each with its own scores button, the New game button, loading and error text.
why.main.jac: Registers the scoreboard walkers, loads global.css and renders the panel.

write_reasoning.services/scores.jac: Backend first: every endpoint is a walker in services/ that visits Team nodes under root and reports them, and add_point takes the team as a has field and visits only the matching node. open_scoreboard seeds the two teams only when root has none.
write_reasoning.components/ScoreboardPanel.jac: The panel owns the team list and spawns open_scoreboard in async can with entry. Its async handlers replace the reported team by jid after add_point and take both reported teams after reset_scores instead of reading again.
write_reasoning.main.jac: Last, main.jac: it imports the walkers and Team from services.scores with no leading dot so they are registered on the server, and returns the panel; one screen needs no router.

plan_call_reasoning: Plan the build: one screen with two saved scores, so a single panel component and a small walker server.
plan_reasoning: One screen: a Scoreboard heading, Home and Away each with a score and a scores button, and a New game button. Each team is a node under root; one walker reads them (seeding on first visit), one adds a point to the named team and one resets both. main.jac last.
plan_summary: Build plan written to .jaccoder/build_plan.json: a single-screen scoreboard, 3 files leaf-first, two team nodes on the server behind three walkers, nova/neutral/amber/inter.
journal:
# Agent journal

## Issues
- Endpoints are walkers so they must live in services/ and be named in main.jac's import, or root spawn gives 405.

## Learnings
- add_point takes the team name as a has field, spawned as root spawn add_point(team=...), and visits only the Team whose name matches.
- The panel swaps the reported team into its list by jid, so the other team's score is left as it was.
- reset_scores reports both teams, so New game sets the whole list from its reports.

## Last Action
Built Scoreboard: a centred card with Home and Away scores, a scores button for each and a New game button, backed by three walkers. The preview shows Home: 2 and Away: 1 after three clicks, keeps them after a reload, and New game puts both back to 0.
final:
Scoreboard is running: each team's button adds a point on the server and New game puts both back to zero. I scored Home twice and Away once, saw Home: 2 and Away: 1, still saw them after a reload, then New game showed Home: 0 and Away: 0.

**Next steps**
- Add a button to take a point back
- Let you rename the teams
- Keep a history of finished games
